references.text: John the Baptist's testimony about Jesus as the Lamb of God unfolds what verse 7 summarizes – he came to testify about the light. See [ref:Joh 1:19-34|John 1:19-34].
Also in [ref:Joh 1:15|John 1:15] John testifies about Christ with similar wording: "John bears witness to him and cries out." This is a direct parallel to the testimony in verse 7.

In [ref:Joh 3:26-36|John 3:26-36] John the Baptist confirms his role as witness and forerunner, not the light itself, but the one who points to the light. The passage ends by linking the testimony to faith: "Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life" – exactly as verse 7 describes the purpose of his mission.

Jesus himself refers to John's testimony in [ref:Joh 5:33-35|John 5:33-35]: "He was a burning and shining lamp, and for a short time you were willing to rejoice in his light." This confirms that John testified about the light.
[ref:Joh 1:9|John 1:9] explains what the light is that John testifies about: "The true light that gives light to everyone was coming into the world."
In [ref:Joh 8:12|John 8:12] Jesus identifies himself as "the light of the world", the very light that John testified about according to verse 7.

Jesus urges people to believe in the light in [ref:Joh 12:36|John 12:36]: "Believe in the light while you have the light, so that you may become children of the light." The purpose of John's testimony was precisely that all should come to faith.

[ref:Jes 49:6|Isaiah 49:6] speaks of the Lord's servant as a light for the nations, so that salvation may reach to the ends of the earth. John's mission was to testify about this light, "so that all might believe through him".
[ref:Mal 3:1|Malachi 3:1] prophesies about the messenger who will prepare the way before the Lord – a prophecy that points directly to John the Baptist's role as forerunner and witness of the light.

In [ref:Apg 19:4|Acts 19:4] Paul summarizes John's work: he preached a baptism of repentance and told the people to believe in the one who was coming after him, that is, Jesus. This confirms the purpose "so that all might believe through him".

The purpose of John's testimony – "so that all might believe" – is reflected throughout the Gospel of John as expressed in [ref:Joh 20:31|John 20:31]: "that you may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name".
[ref:Apg 13:24-25|Acts 13:24-25] describes John's preaching to all Israel and his testimony that the one coming after him was the one they were waiting for – a summary of his witness mission.
